tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

1	# AGENTS.md — geeky-orchestration
2	
3	Guidance for **any** AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Windsurf,
4	Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, or an SDK/LangGraph orchestrator) working with this
5	plugin's plan → execute → track workflow. Claude Code reads this via `@AGENTS.md`;
6	most other CLI agents read `AGENTS.md` natively.
7	
8	## Eval operator readiness
9	
10	This section applies only to operators in the source checkout. Contestant exports deliberately omit `evals/`; exported contestants must follow the canonical authorization and exported skills without looking for these operator files or adding a new approval gate. For source-checkout C0 preparation, read [current readiness](evals/c0-readiness.md) and [lessons learned](evals/lessons-learned.md). Generate fresh offline inventory and verify its exact HEAD, source hashes and prompt hash before a separately authorized live action. Local inventory and mock success grant no launch or telemetry publication authority. Preserve historical evidence and scores. Record desired and observed model/effort by role, the authorization reference, attempt/recovery limits, reserve and existing qualification waiver. Once a particular contestant run is authorized, retain the end-to-end workflow permissions already granted by its canonical prompt.
11	
12	## The workflow
13	
14	1. **spec-research** — research and write `feature-specification.md`.
15	2. **geeky-plan** — create the frozen planning package.
16	3. **plan-review** — validate alignment, coverage, sequencing, and readiness.
17	4. **geeky-status** — read-only status and resumption orientation at any packet stage.
18	5. **geeky-implement** — execute Ready tasks with validation and review gates.
19	6. **impl-review** — review delivered code through three domain-specific lanes.
20	7. **archive** — move completed planning artifacts into the archive structure.
21	
22	Use **geeky-orchestrator** when the requested entry point is unclear or when one
23	agent should administer the lifecycle. It examines repository evidence read-only
24	and recommends a workflow before mutation. Clear, explicit requests route to the
25	best matching skill after prerequisite checks. Material ambiguity is clarified;
26	stages are not auto-chained without end-to-end authorization.
27	
28	Full procedures live in the portable Skills under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
29	
30	## Workflow terminology
31	
32	Use these meanings across skills, briefs and reports. They describe the orchestration
33	domain; retain the target project's own domain language. Existing filenames, schema
34	fields and checkpoint markers remain unchanged.
35	
36	| Term | Meaning |
37	|---|---|
38	| Planning package | Specification, plan, task contracts and tracking artifacts for one approved outcome. "Packet" is an alias; planning folder is its location. |
39	| Workflow stage | A lifecycle activity such as planning, implementation or final implementation review. Numbered "phases" inside a skill are procedure steps, not implementation phases. |
40	| Implementation phase | A group of tasks whose combined requirements are reviewed before advancement. "Wave" means a scheduling group unless the plan explicitly equates it with a phase. |
41	| Task | A bounded unit with an ID, scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria (ACs) and required validation. |
42	| Requirement / AC / Definition of Done | Required outcome or constraint / observable condition for satisfying it / completion conditions for the task. Required tests supply evidence; they do not replace ACs. |
43	| Task contract | The frozen task body and applicable approved requirements. A task brief conveys that contract to a worker. |
44	| Validation | Checks of the work. Validation evidence records what ran or was observed, against which inputs, and the result; a PASS claim alone is not evidence. |
45	| Review | Judgment of evidence against an assigned scope. Task review checks ACs/tests; phase review decides readiness to advance; final implementation review uses `impl-review`. Plan review evaluates the planning package. |
46	| Acceptance | The decision that required outcomes and gates for the stated scope are satisfied. Task Done, phase READY TO ADVANCE and final review PASS have different scopes; none grants release or deployment approval. |
47	| Finding | An evidenced discrepancy. A blocking finding prevents the current contract from being met; an optional improvement is a follow-up. Severity labels retain their review-stage meanings, not an automatic cross-stage mapping. |
48	| Execution batch / review batch | Tasks dispatched together / tasks sharing a reviewer assignment. Each phase has one review batch, the phase review: members wait in In Review until it clears, and each keeps its own verdict. |
49	| Orchestrator / worker / reviewer | Coordinates and accepts work / performs a bounded assignment / evaluates it. `geeky-coder` is the implementation worker; PM describes a planning or phase-review perspective. |
50	
51	## The planning-folder contract
52	
53	**Frozen** (never edit mid-run — they are the contract between plan and implement):
54	`implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`,
55	and every `tasks/Tx-*.md` body. If the plan is genuinely wrong, surface it via the
56	kanban **Blocked** lane + `handoff.md` instead of editing the contract.
57	
58	**Mutable** (update continuously during implement):
59	`kanban.md` (single source of truth for lane status), `handoff.md` (running log),
60	and `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` (per-task notes — these are writable, unlike the task bodies).
61	
62	Record a consequence for another task in that task's notes and in `handoff.md`.
63	
64	## Deterministic quality gates (run these — don't self-report)
65	
66	These replace "I updated the board / the task is done" with fail-stop checks.
67	Every gate: **arguments in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, summary on stdout**,
68	optional `--json` / `-Json`. Each ships paired Python + PowerShell with identical
69	behavior. `geeky.manifest.json` is the machine-readable index of the same list.
70	
71	Paths below are relative to this plugin root (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in Claude Code).
72	Use `python3` where `python` is not on PATH; use `pwsh` (PowerShell 7+) for the `.ps1`.
73	
74	| Gate | When | Python | PowerShell |
75	|---|---|---|---|
76	| Planning-folder valid | start of implement/status | `python scripts/validate-planning-folder.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-planning-folder.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
77	| Task-file schema | end of plan; start of implement | `python scripts/validate-task-schema.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-task-schema.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
78	| Kanban integrity | after every lane move | `python scripts/validate-kanban.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-kanban.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
79	| Definition of Done | in the Done step: move the task to Done, run this gate in the same step, move it back out on failure (D92) | `python scripts/check-dod.py --path "<folder>" --task <ID>` | `pwsh -File scripts/check-dod.ps1 -Path "<folder>" -Task <ID>` |
80	| Commit message | before each commit; pre-planning docs commits use `Tasks: none` | `python scripts/check-commit.py --message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) | `pwsh -File scripts/check-commit.ps1 -Message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) |
81	
82	**Feedback loop:** when a gate exits non-zero, read its output, fix the artifact,
83	and re-run the same gate until it exits 0 before proceeding.
84	
85	## How each agent type runs the gates
86	
87	- **Claude Code:** the frozen-artifact guard fires automatically via
88	  `hooks/hooks.json` (PreToolUse). Run the validators above as explicit steps.
89	- **Other CLI agents (Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Gemini):** add an
90	  equivalent pre-edit/stop hook in your tool's config pointing at
91	  `hooks/guard-planning-contract.{py,ps1}` (it reads tool-call JSON on stdin,
92	  `--mode block` denies via JSON / exit 2). Invoke the validators as shell steps.
93	- **SDK / graph orchestrators (OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph):** call any validator
94	  with `subprocess.run([...])` inside a guardrail / node; raise a tripwire or
95	  `interrupt()` on a non-zero exit.
96	- **Any MCP-capable agent:** a bundled stdio MCP server (`geeky_mcp`, see `mcp/server.py`,
97	  registered in `.mcp.json`) exposes the gates as tools — `geeky_validate_planning_folder`,
98	  `geeky_validate_task_schema`, `geeky_validate_kanban`, `geeky_check_dod`,
99	  `geeky_check_commit`, `geeky_check_frozen_artifact` — for tool-style invocation with
100	  no per-framework hook config. Run it with `uv run --with "mcp>=1.2.0" python mcp/server.py`
101	  (or `pip install mcp && python mcp/server.py`).
102	
103	## Hard rules for implement
104	
105	Never push to a remote. Never `--no-verify`, `--force`, or `--amend`. Respect each
106	task's declared `Dependencies:`. Stop and finalize state (kanban + handoff) when a
107	task moves to Blocked. Verify task validation evidence against the tested revision,
108	commands and results; a coder's bare PASS claim is insufficient. Reuse valid evidence
109	and record the reason for any rerun. Task review checks ACs and defined tests; one reviewer dispatch at
110	phase end gives each task its verdict and the phase verdict. Phase
111	review checks collective requirements and must return READY TO ADVANCE before the
112	next phase starts; that verdict comes from a reviewer subagent whose agent ID is
113	recorded, and the last phase is included. Final implementation review uses `impl-review`.
114	The orchestrator never edits product code or tests; fixes go to `geeky-coder`. Batch independent
115	work and compatible fixes while preserving each task's verdict and resource isolation.

1	# linkvault: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, stdlib only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`, `json`, `argparse`, `urllib`, `secrets`, `hashlib`, `threading`, `signal`); pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `linkvault/` at the workspace root (`linkvault/__init__.py`, `linkvault/__main__.py`); commands run with the workspace root as cwd.
7	- **Entry points:** `python -m linkvault serve ...` (server); `python -m linkvault <client-cmd> ...` (client).
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1 Server start.** `serve` opens or creates the DB, binds 127.0.0.1, then prints exactly one ready line to stdout. Nothing else is ever written to stdout; logs go to stderr.
12	- **R2 Token issuance.** `POST /v1/tokens` with the correct admin key returns a new token. The token is `lv_` followed by 32 lowercase hex characters (`secrets.token_hex(16)`). Only its SHA-256 hex digest is stored.
13	- **R3 Authentication.** Every `/v1/links` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing, malformed or unknown token returns 401.
14	- **R4 Create link.** `POST /v1/links` stores `url` with a custom `slug` or a generated slug, and an optional `expires_in`.
15	- **R5 Slug rules.** Slugs are case-sensitive. A custom slug must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` and must not be `healthz`. A generated slug is 7 characters from `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789`, drawn with `secrets.choice`. It is regenerated if it already exists or is reserved, with up to 5 attempts and then 500. Creating an existing slug returns 409.
16	- **R6 URL rules.** The scheme is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive). `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname` is non-empty. The URL is at most 2048 characters and contains no whitespace or control characters (code points < 0x21 or 0x7F). It is stored and redirected to verbatim.
17	- **R7 Resolve.** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with `Location: <url>` and an empty body. It atomically increments `clicks` and sets `last_clicked_at` to now.
18	- **R8 Missing and expired links.** An unknown slug returns 404. A link with `now >= expires_at` returns 410 and its click count is unchanged. Comparisons use whole seconds.
19	- **R9 List and inspect.** A token can list its own links (expired ones included) and fetch one link with its stats. Another token's link always returns 404, never 403.
20	- **R10 Delete.** A token can delete its own link. Afterwards the slug resolves 404 and is free to reuse.
21	- **R11 Rate limit.** Requests are counted per token in fixed 60-second windows aligned to the Unix epoch (`window_start = now - now % 60`). The limit is `--rate-limit` (default 60) counted requests per window. A request is counted when it reaches the rate-limit step (see precedence in Error handling), whatever its final status. Request number `limit + 1` and later in the same window return 429 with `Retry-After: <window_start + 60 - now>`. Counters are in memory and reset on restart. Redirects, `/healthz` and admin routes are not rate-limited.
22	- **R12 Clock.** "Now" is integer Unix seconds (floor of real time). With `--fake-clock <ISO>`, now is frozen at that instant and changes only through `POST /v1/admin/clock`. The fake clock is not persisted.
23	- **R13 Persistence.** Tokens, links, clicks and `last_clicked_at` survive a restart on the same `--db`.
24	- **R14 Concurrency.** The server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`. N concurrent redirects to one slug leave `clicks == N` exactly.
25	- **R15 Shutdown.** On SIGINT, SIGTERM (POSIX) or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT/SIGBREAK (Windows), the server stops accepting connections, closes the DB and exits 0 within 5 seconds.
26	- **R16 Client.** CLI commands wrap the API. Each prints the response body to stdout, and uses the exit codes below.
27	
28	## Interface contract
29	
30	### Conventions
31	
32	- Timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC with whole seconds. They are stored as INTEGER Unix seconds.
33	- JSON responses are encoded with `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` in UTF-8, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every response sets `Content-Length`; a 204 response has an empty body and MUST send `Content-Length: 0`. Keys appear in exactly the order listed below.
34	- Request `Content-Type` is ignored. The body is read using `Content-Length` (absent means empty), and the maximum is 8192 bytes.
35	- Query strings are ignored on every route. Paths are matched exactly, with no trailing-slash normalisation. Any (method, path) pair not listed below returns 404 `not_found`.
36	- `short_url` is `http://127.0.0.1:<bound port>/<slug>`.
37	
38	**Link object** (key order is fixed): `{"slug", "url", "short_url", "created_at", "expires_at", "clicks", "last_clicked_at"}`. `expires_at` and `last_clicked_at` are `null` until they are set.
39	
40	### Server CLI
41	
42	```
43	python -m linkvault serve --db PATH --admin-key KEY [--port N] [--rate-limit N] [--fake-clock ISO]
44	```
45	
46	| Flag | Rule |
47	|---|---|
48	| `--db` | Required. The file is created if missing, and its parent directory must exist. |
49	| `--admin-key` | Required. Non-empty string. |
50	| `--port` | 0-65535, default 8000. The value 0 binds an OS-chosen free port. |
51	| `--rate-limit` | Integer >= 1, default 60. |
52	| `--fake-clock` | An ISO timestamp in the format above. It enables the admin clock route. |
53	
54	Ready line: `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by a line terminator, which may be `\n` or `\r\n`. It uses the actual bound port, is flushed immediately, and nothing else is written to stdout before it.
55	
56	Exit codes: 0 for a clean shutdown; 2 for a usage error (argparse); 3 if the port cannot be bound or the DB cannot be opened, with a message to stderr.
57	
58	### Endpoints
59	
60	| # | Method and path | Auth | Request body | Success response |
61	|---|---|---|---|---|
62	| E1 | `GET /healthz` | none | none | 200 `{"status":"ok"}` |
63	| E2 | `POST /v1/tokens` | `X-Admin-Key: <key>` | ignored | 201 `{"token":"lv_…","created_at":"…"}` |
64	| E3 | `POST /v1/links` | Bearer | `{"url": str, "slug"?: str, "expires_in"?: int}` | 201, link object |
65	| E4 | `GET /v1/links` | Bearer | none | 200 `{"links":[link…]}` ordered by `created_at` ascending, then `slug` ascending |
66	| E5 | `GET /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 200, link object |
67	| E6 | `DELETE /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 204, empty body |
68	| E7 | `GET /<slug>` | none | none | 302, `Location: <url>`, `Content-Length: 0`, empty body |
69	| E8 | `POST /v1/admin/clock` | `X-Admin-Key` | `{"now": ISO}` | 200 `{"now":"…"}`. The route exists only with `--fake-clock`; otherwise it returns 404. Any valid timestamp is accepted. |
70	
71	E3 body rules:
72	- The body is a JSON object with no extra keys.
73	- `url` is required and must follow R6.
74	- `slug` is optional and must follow R5. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400).
75	- `expires_in` is optional. It is an integer from 1 to 31536000, and `bool` values are rejected. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400). It sets `expires_at = created_at + expires_in`.
76	
77	E8 body rules:
78	- The body must be exactly `{"now": ISO}`, where ISO is a string in the timestamp format above.
79	- A missing `now` key, an extra key, a wrong type or an unparseable timestamp returns 400 `invalid_request`.
80	
81	A wrong or missing admin key on E2 or E8 returns 401. On E5, E6 and E7, a `<slug>` that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` is a route mismatch, so it returns 404 at the route step, before auth.
82	
83	### DB schema (exact)
84	
85	```sql
86	PRAGMA user_version = 1;
87	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
88	  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
89	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
90	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
91	  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
92	  url TEXT NOT NULL,
93	  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
94	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
95	  expires_at INTEGER,
96	  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
97	  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
98	```
99	
100	A click is recorded with one statement: `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`.
101	
102	### Client CLI
103	
104	The server URL comes from `--server URL`, or else the `LINKVAULT_SERVER` environment variable. The token comes from `--token T`, or else `LINKVAULT_TOKEN`. Both options are accepted after the subcommand.
105	
106	| Command | Calls | Stdout on success |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| `token create --admin-key K` | E2 | Response JSON, one line |
109	| `shorten URL [--slug S] [--expires-in N]` | E3 | Response JSON, one line |
110	| `list` | E4 | Response JSON, one line |
111	| `stats SLUG` | E5 | Response JSON, one line |
112	| `delete SLUG` | E6 | Nothing |
113	
114	Output is re-serialised with the server's `json.dumps` settings and ends with `\n`. Client exit codes:
115	
116	| Code | Meaning | Output |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| 0 | 2xx response | as above |
119	| 1 | non-2xx response | Error JSON on stderr, stdout empty |
120	| 2 | usage error, or a missing server or token | Message on stderr |
121	| 3 | connection failure | Message on stderr |
122	
123	## Error handling
124	
125	Every error body has this shape: `{"error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Tests assert `code` only.
126	
127	| Condition | Status | code |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| No route matches the method and path; unknown or foreign slug | 404 | `not_found` |
130	| Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token; bad admin key | 401 | `unauthorized` |
131	| Over the rate limit (adds a `Retry-After` header) | 429 | `rate_limited` |
132	| `Content-Length` > 8192 (the response sets `Connection: close` and the body is not read) | 413 | `payload_too_large` |
133	| Body is not valid UTF-8 JSON, or is not an object | 400 | `invalid_json` |
134	| Schema violation: missing or extra key, wrong type, bad URL, slug, `expires_in` or `now` | 400 | `invalid_request` |
135	| Slug already exists, or is reserved (`healthz`) | 409 | `slug_taken` |
136	| Link expired (E7 only) | 410 | `gone` |
137	| Unhandled exception | 500 | `internal` |
138	
139	Precedence (first failure wins): route 404 → auth 401 → rate limit 429 → size 413 → JSON 400 → validation 400 → resource state 404/409/410.
140	
141	## Acceptance criteria
142	
143	- **AC1 (R1, R15):** `serve --port 0` prints exactly the `LISTENING` line. `GET /healthz` returns 200. SIGINT (or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows) makes it exit 0 within 5 s.
144	- **AC2 (R2):** E2 with the right key returns 201 and a token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`. With a wrong key it returns 401. The DB holds the SHA-256 of the token, never the plaintext.
145	- **AC3 (R3):** E3, E4 and E5 without a valid bearer token return 401 `unauthorized`.
146	- **AC4 (R4, R5):** E3 without `slug` returns a slug matching `^[a-z0-9]{7}$`. A custom `slug` is echoed back. A repeated slug returns 409. `healthz` and `ab` return 409 and 400 respectively.
147	- **AC5 (R6):** `ftp://x`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `http://`, a URL with a space, and a 2049-character URL each return 400 `invalid_request`.
148	- **AC6 (R7):** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with the exact `Location`. A later E5 shows `clicks` 1 and `last_clicked_at` set to now.
149	- **AC7 (R8, R12):** With the fake clock at T and `expires_in=60`, the link resolves 302 at T+59 and 410 at T+60. Its clicks stay at the T+59 value.
150	- **AC8 (R9, R10):** Token B gets 404 on E5 and E6 for token A's slug. A's E4 lists only A's links in order. After E6, `GET /<slug>` returns 404 and the slug can be created again.
151	- **AC9 (R11):** With `--rate-limit 3` and the fake clock at a window start plus 10 s, requests 1-3 succeed. Request 4 returns 429 with `Retry-After: 50`. After the clock moves to the next window, the next request succeeds. Redirects are never limited.
152	- **AC10 (R13):** After a restart on the same DB, tokens still authenticate, and links and clicks are unchanged.
153	- **AC11 (R14):** 50 concurrent `GET /<slug>` requests leave `clicks == 50`.
154	- **AC12 (R16):** `shorten` prints the link JSON and exits 0. A 409 makes it exit 1 with empty stdout. An unreachable server makes it exit 3. A missing token makes it exit 2.

1	# AGENTS.md — geeky-orchestration
2	
3	Guidance for **any** AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Windsurf,
4	Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, or an SDK/LangGraph orchestrator) working with this
5	plugin's plan → execute → track workflow. Claude Code reads this via `@AGENTS.md`;
6	most other CLI agents read `AGENTS.md` natively.
7	
8	## Eval operator readiness
9	
10	This section applies only to operators in the source checkout. Contestant exports deliberately omit `evals/`; exported contestants must follow the canonical authorization and exported skills without looking for these operator files or adding a new approval gate. For source-checkout C0 preparation, read [current readiness](evals/c0-readiness.md) and [lessons learned](evals/lessons-learned.md). Generate fresh offline inventory and verify its exact HEAD, source hashes and prompt hash before a separately authorized live action. Local inventory and mock success grant no launch or telemetry publication authority. Preserve historical evidence and scores. Record desired and observed model/effort by role, the authorization reference, attempt/recovery limits, reserve and existing qualification waiver. Once a particular contestant run is authorized, retain the end-to-end workflow permissions already granted by its canonical prompt.
11	
12	## The workflow
13	
14	1. **spec-research** — research and write `feature-specification.md`.
15	2. **geeky-plan** — create the frozen planning package.
16	3. **plan-review** — validate alignment, coverage, sequencing, and readiness.
17	4. **geeky-status** — read-only status and resumption orientation at any packet stage.
18	5. **geeky-implement** — execute Ready tasks with validation and review gates.
19	6. **impl-review** — review delivered code through three domain-specific lanes.
20	7. **archive** — move completed planning artifacts into the archive structure.
21	
22	Use **geeky-orchestrator** when the requested entry point is unclear or when one
23	agent should administer the lifecycle. It examines repository evidence read-only
24	and recommends a workflow before mutation. Clear, explicit requests route to the
25	best matching skill after prerequisite checks. Material ambiguity is clarified;
26	stages are not auto-chained without end-to-end authorization.
27	
28	Full procedures live in the portable Skills under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
29	
30	## Workflow terminology
31	
32	Use these meanings across skills, briefs and reports. They describe the orchestration
33	domain; retain the target project's own domain language. Existing filenames, schema
34	fields and checkpoint markers remain unchanged.
35	
36	| Term | Meaning |
37	|---|---|
38	| Planning package | Specification, plan, task contracts and tracking artifacts for one approved outcome. "Packet" is an alias; planning folder is its location. |
39	| Workflow stage | A lifecycle activity such as planning, implementation or final implementation review. Numbered "phases" inside a skill are procedure steps, not implementation phases. |
40	| Implementation phase | A group of tasks whose combined requirements are reviewed before advancement. "Wave" means a scheduling group unless the plan explicitly equates it with a phase. |
41	| Task | A bounded unit with an ID, scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria (ACs) and required validation. |
42	| Requirement / AC / Definition of Done | Required outcome or constraint / observable condition for satisfying it / completion conditions for the task. Required tests supply evidence; they do not replace ACs. |
43	| Task contract | The frozen task body and applicable approved requirements. A task brief conveys that contract to a worker. |
44	| Validation | Checks of the work. Validation evidence records what ran or was observed, against which inputs, and the result; a PASS claim alone is not evidence. |
45	| Review | Judgment of evidence against an assigned scope. Task review checks ACs/tests; phase review decides readiness to advance; final implementation review uses `impl-review`. Plan review evaluates the planning package. |
46	| Acceptance | The decision that required outcomes and gates for the stated scope are satisfied. Task Done, phase READY TO ADVANCE and final review PASS have different scopes; none grants release or deployment approval. |
47	| Finding | An evidenced discrepancy. A blocking finding prevents the current contract from being met; an optional improvement is a follow-up. Severity labels retain their review-stage meanings, not an automatic cross-stage mapping. |
48	| Execution batch / review batch | Tasks dispatched together / tasks sharing a reviewer assignment. Each phase has one review batch, the phase review: members wait in In Review until it clears, and each keeps its own verdict. |
49	| Orchestrator / worker / reviewer | Coordinates and accepts work / performs a bounded assignment / evaluates it. `geeky-coder` is the implementation worker; PM describes a planning or phase-review perspective. |
50	
51	## The planning-folder contract
52	
53	**Frozen** (never edit mid-run — they are the contract between plan and implement):
54	`implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`,
55	and every `tasks/Tx-*.md` body. If the plan is genuinely wrong, surface it via the
56	kanban **Blocked** lane + `handoff.md` instead of editing the contract.
57	
58	**Mutable** (update continuously during implement):
59	`kanban.md` (single source of truth for lane status), `handoff.md` (running log),
60	and `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` (per-task notes — these are writable, unlike the task bodies).
61	
62	Record a consequence for another task in that task's notes and in `handoff.md`.
63	
64	## Deterministic quality gates (run these — don't self-report)
65	
66	These replace "I updated the board / the task is done" with fail-stop checks.
67	Every gate: **arguments in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, summary on stdout**,
68	optional `--json` / `-Json`. Each ships paired Python + PowerShell with identical
69	behavior. `geeky.manifest.json` is the machine-readable index of the same list.
70	
71	Paths below are relative to this plugin root (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in Claude Code).
72	Use `python3` where `python` is not on PATH; use `pwsh` (PowerShell 7+) for the `.ps1`.
73	
74	| Gate | When | Python | PowerShell |
75	|---|---|---|---|
76	| Planning-folder valid | start of implement/status | `python scripts/validate-planning-folder.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-planning-folder.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
77	| Task-file schema | end of plan; start of implement | `python scripts/validate-task-schema.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-task-schema.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
78	| Kanban integrity | after every lane move | `python scripts/validate-kanban.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-kanban.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
79	| Definition of Done | in the Done step: move the task to Done, run this gate in the same step, move it back out on failure (D92) | `python scripts/check-dod.py --path "<folder>" --task <ID>` | `pwsh -File scripts/check-dod.ps1 -Path "<folder>" -Task <ID>` |
80	| Commit message | before each commit; pre-planning docs commits use `Tasks: none` | `python scripts/check-commit.py --message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) | `pwsh -File scripts/check-commit.ps1 -Message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) |
81	
82	**Feedback loop:** when a gate exits non-zero, read its output, fix the artifact,
83	and re-run the same gate until it exits 0 before proceeding.
84	
85	## How each agent type runs the gates
86	
87	- **Claude Code:** the frozen-artifact guard fires automatically via
88	  `hooks/hooks.json` (PreToolUse). Run the validators above as explicit steps.
89	- **Other CLI agents (Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Gemini):** add an
90	  equivalent pre-edit/stop hook in your tool's config pointing at
91	  `hooks/guard-planning-contract.{py,ps1}` (it reads tool-call JSON on stdin,
92	  `--mode block` denies via JSON / exit 2). Invoke the validators as shell steps.
93	- **SDK / graph orchestrators (OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph):** call any validator
94	  with `subprocess.run([...])` inside a guardrail / node; raise a tripwire or
95	  `interrupt()` on a non-zero exit.
96	- **Any MCP-capable agent:** a bundled stdio MCP server (`geeky_mcp`, see `mcp/server.py`,
97	  registered in `.mcp.json`) exposes the gates as tools — `geeky_validate_planning_folder`,
98	  `geeky_validate_task_schema`, `geeky_validate_kanban`, `geeky_check_dod`,
99	  `geeky_check_commit`, `geeky_check_frozen_artifact` — for tool-style invocation with
100	  no per-framework hook config. Run it with `uv run --with "mcp>=1.2.0" python mcp/server.py`
101	  (or `pip install mcp && python mcp/server.py`).
102	
103	## Hard rules for implement
104	
105	Never push to a remote. Never `--no-verify`, `--force`, or `--amend`. Respect each
106	task's declared `Dependencies:`. Stop and finalize state (kanban + handoff) when a
107	task moves to Blocked. Verify task validation evidence against the tested revision,
108	commands and results; a coder's bare PASS claim is insufficient. Reuse valid evidence
109	and record the reason for any rerun. Task review checks ACs and defined tests; one reviewer dispatch at
110	phase end gives each task its verdict and the phase verdict. Phase
111	review checks collective requirements and must return READY TO ADVANCE before the
112	next phase starts; that verdict comes from a reviewer subagent whose agent ID is
113	recorded, and the last phase is included. Final implementation review uses `impl-review`.
114	The orchestrator never edits product code or tests; fixes go to `geeky-coder`. Batch independent
115	work and compatible fixes while preserving each task's verdict and resource isolation.

1	# linkvault: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, stdlib only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`, `json`, `argparse`, `urllib`, `secrets`, `hashlib`, `threading`, `signal`); pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `linkvault/` at the workspace root (`linkvault/__init__.py`, `linkvault/__main__.py`); commands run with the workspace root as cwd.
7	- **Entry points:** `python -m linkvault serve ...` (server); `python -m linkvault <client-cmd> ...` (client).
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1 Server start.** `serve` opens or creates the DB, binds 127.0.0.1, then prints exactly one ready line to stdout. Nothing else is ever written to stdout; logs go to stderr.
12	- **R2 Token issuance.** `POST /v1/tokens` with the correct admin key returns a new token. The token is `lv_` followed by 32 lowercase hex characters (`secrets.token_hex(16)`). Only its SHA-256 hex digest is stored.
13	- **R3 Authentication.** Every `/v1/links` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing, malformed or unknown token returns 401.
14	- **R4 Create link.** `POST /v1/links` stores `url` with a custom `slug` or a generated slug, and an optional `expires_in`.
15	- **R5 Slug rules.** Slugs are case-sensitive. A custom slug must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` and must not be `healthz`. A generated slug is 7 characters from `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789`, drawn with `secrets.choice`. It is regenerated if it already exists or is reserved, with up to 5 attempts and then 500. Creating an existing slug returns 409.
16	- **R6 URL rules.** The scheme is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive). `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname` is non-empty. The URL is at most 2048 characters and contains no whitespace or control characters (code points < 0x21 or 0x7F). It is stored and redirected to verbatim.
17	- **R7 Resolve.** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with `Location: <url>` and an empty body. It atomically increments `clicks` and sets `last_clicked_at` to now.
18	- **R8 Missing and expired links.** An unknown slug returns 404. A link with `now >= expires_at` returns 410 and its click count is unchanged. Comparisons use whole seconds.
19	- **R9 List and inspect.** A token can list its own links (expired ones included) and fetch one link with its stats. Another token's link always returns 404, never 403.
20	- **R10 Delete.** A token can delete its own link. Afterwards the slug resolves 404 and is free to reuse.
21	- **R11 Rate limit.** Requests are counted per token in fixed 60-second windows aligned to the Unix epoch (`window_start = now - now % 60`). The limit is `--rate-limit` (default 60) counted requests per window. A request is counted when it reaches the rate-limit step (see precedence in Error handling), whatever its final status. Request number `limit + 1` and later in the same window return 429 with `Retry-After: <window_start + 60 - now>`. Counters are in memory and reset on restart. Redirects, `/healthz` and admin routes are not rate-limited.
22	- **R12 Clock.** "Now" is integer Unix seconds (floor of real time). With `--fake-clock <ISO>`, now is frozen at that instant and changes only through `POST /v1/admin/clock`. The fake clock is not persisted.
23	- **R13 Persistence.** Tokens, links, clicks and `last_clicked_at` survive a restart on the same `--db`.
24	- **R14 Concurrency.** The server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`. N concurrent redirects to one slug leave `clicks == N` exactly.
25	- **R15 Shutdown.** On SIGINT, SIGTERM (POSIX) or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT/SIGBREAK (Windows), the server stops accepting connections, closes the DB and exits 0 within 5 seconds.
26	- **R16 Client.** CLI commands wrap the API. Each prints the response body to stdout, and uses the exit codes below.
27	
28	## Interface contract
29	
30	### Conventions
31	
32	- Timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC with whole seconds. They are stored as INTEGER Unix seconds.
33	- JSON responses are encoded with `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` in UTF-8, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every response sets `Content-Length`; a 204 response has an empty body and MUST send `Content-Length: 0`. Keys appear in exactly the order listed below.
34	- Request `Content-Type` is ignored. The body is read using `Content-Length` (absent means empty), and the maximum is 8192 bytes.
35	- Query strings are ignored on every route. Paths are matched exactly, with no trailing-slash normalisation. Any (method, path) pair not listed below returns 404 `not_found`.
36	- `short_url` is `http://127.0.0.1:<bound port>/<slug>`.
37	
38	**Link object** (key order is fixed): `{"slug", "url", "short_url", "created_at", "expires_at", "clicks", "last_clicked_at"}`. `expires_at` and `last_clicked_at` are `null` until they are set.
39	
40	### Server CLI
41	
42	```
43	python -m linkvault serve --db PATH --admin-key KEY [--port N] [--rate-limit N] [--fake-clock ISO]
44	```
45	
46	| Flag | Rule |
47	|---|---|
48	| `--db` | Required. The file is created if missing, and its parent directory must exist. |
49	| `--admin-key` | Required. Non-empty string. |
50	| `--port` | 0-65535, default 8000. The value 0 binds an OS-chosen free port. |
51	| `--rate-limit` | Integer >= 1, default 60. |
52	| `--fake-clock` | An ISO timestamp in the format above. It enables the admin clock route. |
53	
54	Ready line: `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by a line terminator, which may be `\n` or `\r\n`. It uses the actual bound port, is flushed immediately, and nothing else is written to stdout before it.
55	
56	Exit codes: 0 for a clean shutdown; 2 for a usage error (argparse); 3 if the port cannot be bound or the DB cannot be opened, with a message to stderr.
57	
58	### Endpoints
59	
60	| # | Method and path | Auth | Request body | Success response |
61	|---|---|---|---|---|
62	| E1 | `GET /healthz` | none | none | 200 `{"status":"ok"}` |
63	| E2 | `POST /v1/tokens` | `X-Admin-Key: <key>` | ignored | 201 `{"token":"lv_…","created_at":"…"}` |
64	| E3 | `POST /v1/links` | Bearer | `{"url": str, "slug"?: str, "expires_in"?: int}` | 201, link object |
65	| E4 | `GET /v1/links` | Bearer | none | 200 `{"links":[link…]}` ordered by `created_at` ascending, then `slug` ascending |
66	| E5 | `GET /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 200, link object |
67	| E6 | `DELETE /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 204, empty body |
68	| E7 | `GET /<slug>` | none | none | 302, `Location: <url>`, `Content-Length: 0`, empty body |
69	| E8 | `POST /v1/admin/clock` | `X-Admin-Key` | `{"now": ISO}` | 200 `{"now":"…"}`. The route exists only with `--fake-clock`; otherwise it returns 404. Any valid timestamp is accepted. |
70	
71	E3 body rules:
72	- The body is a JSON object with no extra keys.
73	- `url` is required and must follow R6.
74	- `slug` is optional and must follow R5. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400).
75	- `expires_in` is optional. It is an integer from 1 to 31536000, and `bool` values are rejected. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400). It sets `expires_at = created_at + expires_in`.
76	
77	E8 body rules:
78	- The body must be exactly `{"now": ISO}`, where ISO is a string in the timestamp format above.
79	- A missing `now` key, an extra key, a wrong type or an unparseable timestamp returns 400 `invalid_request`.
80	
81	A wrong or missing admin key on E2 or E8 returns 401. On E5, E6 and E7, a `<slug>` that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` is a route mismatch, so it returns 404 at the route step, before auth.
82	
83	### DB schema (exact)
84	
85	```sql
86	PRAGMA user_version = 1;
87	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
88	  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
89	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
90	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
91	  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
92	  url TEXT NOT NULL,
93	  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
94	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
95	  expires_at INTEGER,
96	  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
97	  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
98	```
99	
100	A click is recorded with one statement: `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`.
101	
102	### Client CLI
103	
104	The server URL comes from `--server URL`, or else the `LINKVAULT_SERVER` environment variable. The token comes from `--token T`, or else `LINKVAULT_TOKEN`. Both options are accepted after the subcommand.
105	
106	| Command | Calls | Stdout on success |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| `token create --admin-key K` | E2 | Response JSON, one line |
109	| `shorten URL [--slug S] [--expires-in N]` | E3 | Response JSON, one line |
110	| `list` | E4 | Response JSON, one line |
111	| `stats SLUG` | E5 | Response JSON, one line |
112	| `delete SLUG` | E6 | Nothing |
113	
114	Output is re-serialised with the server's `json.dumps` settings and ends with `\n`. Client exit codes:
115	
116	| Code | Meaning | Output |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| 0 | 2xx response | as above |
119	| 1 | non-2xx response | Error JSON on stderr, stdout empty |
120	| 2 | usage error, or a missing server or token | Message on stderr |
121	| 3 | connection failure | Message on stderr |
122	
123	## Error handling
124	
125	Every error body has this shape: `{"error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Tests assert `code` only.
126	
127	| Condition | Status | code |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| No route matches the method and path; unknown or foreign slug | 404 | `not_found` |
130	| Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token; bad admin key | 401 | `unauthorized` |
131	| Over the rate limit (adds a `Retry-After` header) | 429 | `rate_limited` |
132	| `Content-Length` > 8192 (the response sets `Connection: close` and the body is not read) | 413 | `payload_too_large` |
133	| Body is not valid UTF-8 JSON, or is not an object | 400 | `invalid_json` |
134	| Schema violation: missing or extra key, wrong type, bad URL, slug, `expires_in` or `now` | 400 | `invalid_request` |
135	| Slug already exists, or is reserved (`healthz`) | 409 | `slug_taken` |
136	| Link expired (E7 only) | 410 | `gone` |
137	| Unhandled exception | 500 | `internal` |
138	
139	Precedence (first failure wins): route 404 → auth 401 → rate limit 429 → size 413 → JSON 400 → validation 400 → resource state 404/409/410.
140	
141	## Acceptance criteria
142	
143	- **AC1 (R1, R15):** `serve --port 0` prints exactly the `LISTENING` line. `GET /healthz` returns 200. SIGINT (or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows) makes it exit 0 within 5 s.
144	- **AC2 (R2):** E2 with the right key returns 201 and a token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`. With a wrong key it returns 401. The DB holds the SHA-256 of the token, never the plaintext.
145	- **AC3 (R3):** E3, E4 and E5 without a valid bearer token return 401 `unauthorized`.
146	- **AC4 (R4, R5):** E3 without `slug` returns a slug matching `^[a-z0-9]{7}$`. A custom `slug` is echoed back. A repeated slug returns 409. `healthz` and `ab` return 409 and 400 respectively.
147	- **AC5 (R6):** `ftp://x`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `http://`, a URL with a space, and a 2049-character URL each return 400 `invalid_request`.
148	- **AC6 (R7):** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with the exact `Location`. A later E5 shows `clicks` 1 and `last_clicked_at` set to now.
149	- **AC7 (R8, R12):** With the fake clock at T and `expires_in=60`, the link resolves 302 at T+59 and 410 at T+60. Its clicks stay at the T+59 value.
150	- **AC8 (R9, R10):** Token B gets 404 on E5 and E6 for token A's slug. A's E4 lists only A's links in order. After E6, `GET /<slug>` returns 404 and the slug can be created again.
151	- **AC9 (R11):** With `--rate-limit 3` and the fake clock at a window start plus 10 s, requests 1-3 succeed. Request 4 returns 429 with `Retry-After: 50`. After the clock moves to the next window, the next request succeeds. Redirects are never limited.
152	- **AC10 (R13):** After a restart on the same DB, tokens still authenticate, and links and clicks are unchanged.
153	- **AC11 (R14):** 50 concurrent `GET /<slug>` requests leave `clicks == 50`.
154	- **AC12 (R16):** `shorten` prints the link JSON and exits 0. A 409 makes it exit 1 with empty stdout. An unreachable server makes it exit 3. A missing token makes it exit 2.

1	"""Validation, wire values, and synchronized in-memory request state."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
6	import json
7	import math
8	import re
9	import threading
10	import time
11	from urllib.parse import urlsplit
12	
13	
14	class APIError(Exception):
15	    """An expected API failure; unexpected exceptions remain internal errors."""
16	
17	    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str, headers: dict | None = None):
18	        super().__init__(message)
19	        self.status = status
20	        self.code = code
21	        self.message = message
22	        self.headers = {} if headers is None else headers
23	
24	    def body(self) -> dict:
25	        return {"error": {"code": self.code, "message": self.message}}
26	
27	
28	def json_bytes(value: object) -> bytes:
29	    return json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True).encode("utf-8")
30	
31	
32	def _reject_constant(value: str) -> None:
33	    raise ValueError("Non-JSON number: " + value)
34	
35	
36	def decode_json(body: bytes) -> dict:
37	    """Decode an object only; request size/auth/route checks belong to HTTP."""
38	    try:
39	        value = json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"), parse_constant=_reject_constant)
40	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, RecursionError):
41	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_json", "Expected a UTF-8 JSON object") from None
42	    if not isinstance(value, dict):
43	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_json", "Expected a JSON object")
44	    return value
45	
46	
47	_EPOCH = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
48	_TIMESTAMP = re.compile(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z")
49	_SLUG = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}")
50	
51	
52	def parse_timestamp(value: str) -> int:
53	    if not isinstance(value, str) or _TIMESTAMP.fullmatch(value) is None:
54	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid UTC timestamp")
55	    try:
56	        instant = datetime(
57	            int(value[:4]), int(value[5:7]), int(value[8:10]),
58	            int(value[11:13]), int(value[14:16]), int(value[17:19]),
59	            tzinfo=timezone.utc,
60	        )
61	    except ValueError:
62	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid UTC timestamp") from None
63	    return (instant - _EPOCH) // timedelta(seconds=1)
64	
65	
66	def format_timestamp(value: int) -> str:
67	    instant = _EPOCH + timedelta(seconds=value)
68	    return (
69	        f"{instant.year:04d}-{instant.month:02d}-{instant.day:02d}"
70	        f"T{instant.hour:02d}:{instant.minute:02d}:{instant.second:02d}Z"
71	    )
72	
73	
74	def valid_slug(value: object) -> bool:
75	    """Syntax only: the reserved healthz slug is a later resource conflict."""
76	    return isinstance(value, str) and _SLUG.fullmatch(value) is not None
77	
78	
79	def validate_url(value: str) -> str:
80	    if (
81	        not isinstance(value, str) or not value or len(value) > 2048
82	        or any(character.isspace() or ord(character) < 0x21 or ord(character) == 0x7F
83	               for character in value)
84	    ):
85	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid URL")
86	    try:
87	        parts = urlsplit(value)
88	        valid = parts.scheme.lower() in ("http", "https") and bool(parts.hostname)
89	    except ValueError:
90	        valid = False
91	    if not valid:
92	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid URL")
93	    return value
94	
95	
96	def validate_create(body: dict) -> dict:
97	    if (
98	        not isinstance(body, dict) or "url" not in body
99	        or set(body) - {"url", "slug", "expires_in"}
100	    ):
101	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid link fields")
102	    validate_url(body["url"])
103	    if "slug" in body and not valid_slug(body["slug"]):
104	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid slug")
105	    if "expires_in" in body and (
106	        type(body["expires_in"]) is not int or not 1 <= body["expires_in"] <= 31536000
107	    ):
108	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid expires_in")
109	    return body
110	
111	
112	def validate_clock(body: dict) -> int:
113	    if not isinstance(body, dict) or set(body) != {"now"}:
114	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Expected only now")
115	    return parse_timestamp(body["now"])
116	
117	
118	class Clock:
119	    """None selects real time; fake_now and set() use parsed integer seconds."""
120	
121	    def __init__(self, fake_now: int | None = None):
122	        self._fake_now = fake_now
123	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
124	        self.is_fake = fake_now is not None
125	
126	    def now(self) -> int:
127	        with self._lock:
128	            return self._fake_now if self.is_fake else math.floor(time.time())
129	
130	    def set(self, now: int) -> int:
131	        with self._lock:
132	            if not self.is_fake:
133	                raise APIError(404, "not_found", "Fake clock is disabled")
134	            self._fake_now = now
135	            return now
136	
137	
138	class RateLimiter:
139	    """Count every check, retaining historical windows for backward fake time."""
140	
141	    def __init__(self, limit: int = 60):
142	        if type(limit) is not int or limit < 1:
143	            raise ValueError("Rate limit must be a positive integer")
144	        self._limit = limit
145	        self._counts: dict[tuple[str, int], int] = {}
146	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
147	
148	    def check(self, token_hash: str, now: int) -> None:
149	        window_start = now - now % 60
150	        key = (token_hash, window_start)
151	        with self._lock:
152	            count = self._counts.get(key, 0) + 1
153	            self._counts[key] = count
154	        if count > self._limit:
155	            raise APIError(
156	                429, "rate_limited", "Rate limit exceeded",
157	                {"Retry-After": str(window_start + 60 - now)},
158	            )

7	## Frozen internal API for T2/T3
8	
9	`linkvault.domain` exports the following small interface (all runtime dependencies are stdlib):
10	
11	- `APIError(status: int, code: str, message: str, headers: dict | None = None)`: exception with `.status`, `.code`, `.message`, `.headers`; `.body() -> dict` returns ordered `{"error":{"code":...,"message":...}}`. Headers default to a new empty dict.
12	- `json_bytes(value: object) -> bytes`: exact compact `json.dumps(..., separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` plus UTF-8 encoding; insertion order is retained. HTTP supplies Content-Type/Content-Length.
13	- `decode_json(body: bytes) -> dict`: UTF-8 JSON object only; raises 400 `invalid_json` for invalid UTF-8/JSON/nonobjects, including non-JSON NaN/Infinity. Request size/auth/rate checks are deliberately outside this function.
14	- `parse_timestamp(value: str) -> int`: strict ASCII timestamp/calendar validation, UTC integer seconds, including years 0001–9999 and negative epochs; raises 400 `invalid_request`.
15	- `format_timestamp(value: int) -> str`: integer seconds to exact UTC four-digit-year timestamp. Out-of-four-digit-range arithmetic raises an ordinary overflow exception, which HTTP translates to 500 `internal`; no new timestamp format or input restriction is invented.
16	- `valid_slug(value: object) -> bool`: full-match ASCII syntax only. T2 uses it for E5/E6/E7 route matching before auth. `healthz` is syntactically valid: its creation conflict is checked later by storage.
17	- `validate_url(value: str) -> str`: validates original URL and returns it unchanged; no `.port` access or normalization; violations raise 400 `invalid_request`.
18	- `validate_create(body: dict) -> dict`: validates all E3 fields and returns the same unmodified dict. Unknown/missing/wrong/null fields raise 400 `invalid_request`. Does not check slug resource state. Storage invokes this itself.
19	- `validate_clock(body: dict) -> int`: exactly `{"now": ISO}` to parsed integer seconds; raises 400 `invalid_request` on schema/timestamp errors.
20	- `Clock(fake_now: int | None = None)`: `.is_fake: bool`, `.now() -> int`, `.set(now: int) -> int`. `None` means real floor(time.time()); integer zero is fake epoch, not disabled. Access/mutation is locked. `.set()` accepts already-parsed integer seconds and supports backward changes; real mode raises 404 `not_found`. Clock state is never persisted.
21	- `RateLimiter(limit: int = 60)`: `.check(token_hash: str, now: int) -> None`, synchronized counters keyed by `(token_hash, now - now % 60)`. Count every call, including rejected calls. Raises 429 `rate_limited`, `.headers == {"Retry-After": "<whole seconds>"}` after the limit. Historical windows survive backward fake-clock moves; a new instance resets counters. Invalid constructor limit raises ordinary `ValueError` (CLI validates configuration first).
22	
23	**Fake-clock coordination:** T3 should use `parse_timestamp` as the basis for an argparse type and store integer seconds in `args.fake_clock` (default `None`). Convert `APIError` from this argument type into `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` so invalid CLI input exits 2. T2 constructs `Clock(args.fake_clock)`; E8 uses `clock.set(validate_clock(decoded_body))`, then `format_timestamp` for its response. If T2 also accepts an unvalidated string in `run(args)`, parse it before constructing Clock. Snapshot `now = clock.now()` once per request and pass that same integer to limiter/storage.
24	
25	`linkvault.storage.Storage(path: str)` opens/creates the exact schema using a single connection with `check_same_thread=False`; all DB access/transaction completion and closure are serialized by one lock. Parent directories are not created. Exported instance methods:
26	
27	- `issue_token(now: int) -> dict`: ordered `token,created_at`; `lv_` + `secrets.token_hex(16)`; stores only full-token SHA-256 digest and integer timestamp; committed before return.
28	- `authenticate(token: str) -> str`: takes the raw token, not the Authorization header; returns its digest as an opaque owner/rate key. Malformed/unknown tokens raise 401 `unauthorized`. T2 must enforce exact single-space `Bearer <token>` header syntax before calling this.
29	- `create_link(token_hash: str, body: dict, now: int, base_url: str) -> dict`: validates complete E3 schema before checking state, generates at most five seven-character candidates using exact `secrets.choice` alphabet, commits, and returns the ordered link object. Custom duplicate/reserved lowercase `healthz` raises 409 `slug_taken`; generation exhaustion raises 500 `internal`. Expired links still occupy slugs.
30	- `list_links(token_hash: str, base_url: str) -> dict`: ordered `{"links": [...]}` including expired links, sorted by created_at then binary/case-sensitive slug.
31	- `get_link(token_hash: str, slug: str, base_url: str) -> dict`: ordered link object; unknown/foreign resource raises 404 `not_found`.
32	- `delete_link(token_hash: str, slug: str) -> None`: committed deletion; unknown/foreign resource raises 404 `not_found`; slug immediately reusable. T2 sends empty 204.
33	- `resolve(slug: str, now: int) -> str`: verbatim URL after locked lookup/expiry/exact prescribed increment SQL/commit. Unknown raises 404 `not_found`; `now >= expires_at` raises 410 `gone` without mutation. T2 sends empty 302 with exact Location. No rate limiting occurs in storage.
34	- `close() -> None`: locked connection closure; callers stop/drain request work before closing.
35	
36	`base_url` must be the actual bound origin, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:43210` without a trailing slash. Every returned link uses ordered keys `slug,url,short_url,created_at,expires_at,clicks,last_clicked_at`, with nullable fields represented by `None`. Owners are digests obtained from `authenticate`, not user-supplied identities. No database row/connection escapes the public methods.

38	## Exception/error translation and precedence
39	
40	T2 catches `APIError` and sends `error.status`, `error.headers`, `json_bytes(error.body())`; unexpected exceptions become 500 `internal` and must not expose exception text/DB details. SQLite open/initialization exceptions deliberately propagate for `server.run` startup handling (stderr, exit 3). Other SQLite errors also propagate as unexpected internal errors, not misleading 409 conflicts; failed mutation transactions roll back. T3 translates timestamp/configuration validation failures into argparse usage errors (exit 2), not HTTP JSON.

42	The caller owns route404 → auth401 → limiter429 → size413 → decode400 → schema400 → resource404/409/410. Call limiter exactly once per authenticated link request after route/auth and before body size/decode/storage, regardless of later status. Do not call it for admin, health or redirects. Storage does not enforce route matching or HTTP header grammar. Raw schema dictionaries are validated inside create; E8 validation is explicit through `validate_clock`.

9	## Unicode Location wire decision
10	
11	Valid URLs are not restricted beyond T1 R6 validation. Storage and JSON retain the original URL. For redirect Location, original Latin-1-compatible values use their original Latin-1 bytes (preserving stdlib header compatibility); values containing non-Latin-1 characters use the original value's UTF-8 bytes, emitted through the stdlib header writer without percent escaping, IDNA, normalization, or replacement. A client that decodes every header as Latin-1 must recover the raw octets and decode UTF-8 for this latter case. The contract does not specify a Unicode header charset. 52	def parse_timestamp(value: str) -> int:
53	    if not isinstance(value, str) or _TIMESTAMP.fullmatch(value) is None:
54	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid UTC timestamp")
55	    try:
56	        instant = datetime(
57	            int(value[:4]), int(value[5:7]), int(value[8:10]),
58	            int(value[11:13]), int(value[14:16]), int(value[17:19]),
59	            tzinfo=timezone.utc,
60	        )
61	    except ValueError:
62	        raise APIError(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid UTC timestamp") from None
63	    return (instant - _EPOCH) // timedelta(seconds=1)

70	        f"T{instant.hour:02d}:{instant.minute:02d}:{instant.second:02d}Z"

118	class Clock:
119	    """None selects real time; fake_now and set() use parsed integer seconds."""
120	
121	    def __init__(self, fake_now: int | None = None):
122	        self._fake_now = fake_now
123	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
124	        self.is_fake = fake_now is not None
125	
126	    def now(self) -> int:
127	        with self._lock:
128	            return self._fake_now if self.is_fake else math.floor(time.time())
129	
130	    def set(self, now: int) -> int:
131	        with self._lock:
132	            if not self.is_fake:
133	                raise APIError(404, "not_found", "Fake clock is disabled")
134	            self._fake_now = now
135	            return now

138	class RateLimiter:
139	    """Count every check, retaining historical windows for backward fake time."""
140	
141	    def __init__(self, limit: int = 60):
142	        if type(limit) is not int or limit < 1:
143	            raise ValueError("Rate limit must be a positive integer")
144	        self._limit = limit
145	        self._counts: dict[tuple[str, int], int] = {}
146	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
147	
148	    def check(self, token_hash: str, now: int) -> None:
149	        window_start = now - now % 60
150	        key = (token_hash, window_start)
151	        with self._lock:
152	            count = self._counts.get(key, 0) + 1
153	            self._counts[key] = count
154	        if count > self._limit:
155	            raise APIError(
156	                429, "rate_limited", "Rate limit exceeded",
157	                {"Retry-After": str(window_start + 60 - now)},
158	            )

30	def request(port, method, target, body=None, headers=None):
31	    connection = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", port, timeout=4)
32	    try:
33	        connection.request(method, target, body=body, headers=headers or {})
34	        response = connection.getresponse()
35	        payload = response.read()
36	        assert int(response.getheader("Content-Length")) == len(payload)
37	        if payload:
38	            assert response.getheader("Content-Type") == "application/json"
39	            assert json_bytes(json.loads(payload)) == payload
40	        return response.status, dict(response.getheaders()), payload
41	    finally:
42	        connection.close()

45	def raw_request(port, payload):
46	    with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=4) as connection:
47	        connection.sendall(payload)
48	        chunks = []
49	        while True:
50	            chunk = connection.recv(65536)
51	            if not chunk:
52	                break
53	            chunks.append(chunk)
54	    head, body = b"".join(chunks).split(b"\r\n\r\n", 1)
55	    lines = head.split(b"\r\n")
56	    headers = dict(line.split(b": ", 1) for line in lines[1:])
57	    assert int(headers[b"Content-Length"]) == len(body)
58	    return int(lines[0].split()[1]), headers, body

7	## Frozen internal API for T2/T3
8	
9	`linkvault.domain` exports the following small interface (all runtime dependencies are stdlib):
10	
11	- `APIError(status: int, code: str, message: str, headers: dict | None = None)`: exception with `.status`, `.code`, `.message`, `.headers`; `.body() -> dict` returns ordered `{"error":{"code":...,"message":...}}`. Headers default to a new empty dict.
12	- `json_bytes(value: object) -> bytes`: exact compact `json.dumps(..., separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` plus UTF-8 encoding; insertion order is retained. HTTP supplies Content-Type/Content-Length.
13	- `decode_json(body: bytes) -> dict`: UTF-8 JSON object only; raises 400 `invalid_json` for invalid UTF-8/JSON/nonobjects, including non-JSON NaN/Infinity. Request size/auth/rate checks are deliberately outside this function.
14	- `parse_timestamp(value: str) -> int`: strict ASCII timestamp/calendar validation, UTC integer seconds, including years 0001–9999 and negative epochs; raises 400 `invalid_request`.
15	- `format_timestamp(value: int) -> str`: integer seconds to exact UTC four-digit-year timestamp. Out-of-four-digit-range arithmetic raises an ordinary overflow exception, which HTTP translates to 500 `internal`; no new timestamp format or input restriction is invented.
16	- `valid_slug(value: object) -> bool`: full-match ASCII syntax only. T2 uses it for E5/E6/E7 route matching before auth. `healthz` is syntactically valid: its creation conflict is checked later by storage.
17	- `validate_url(value: str) -> str`: validates original URL and returns it unchanged; no `.port` access or normalization; violations raise 400 `invalid_request`.
18	- `validate_create(body: dict) -> dict`: validates all E3 fields and returns the same unmodified dict. Unknown/missing/wrong/null fields raise 400 `invalid_request`. Does not check slug resource state. Storage invokes this itself.
19	- `validate_clock(body: dict) -> int`: exactly `{"now": ISO}` to parsed integer seconds; raises 400 `invalid_request` on schema/timestamp errors.
20	- `Clock(fake_now: int | None = None)`: `.is_fake: bool`, `.now() -> int`, `.set(now: int) -> int`. `None` means real floor(time.time()); integer zero is fake epoch, not disabled. Access/mutation is locked. `.set()` accepts already-parsed integer seconds and supports backward changes; real mode raises 404 `not_found`. Clock state is never persisted.
21	- `RateLimiter(limit: int = 60)`: `.check(token_hash: str, now: int) -> None`, synchronized counters keyed by `(token_hash, now - now % 60)`. Count every call, including rejected calls. Raises 429 `rate_limited`, `.headers == {"Retry-After": "<whole seconds>"}` after the limit. Historical windows survive backward fake-clock moves; a new instance resets counters. Invalid constructor limit raises ordinary `ValueError` (CLI validates configuration first).
22	
23	**Fake-clock coordination:** T3 should use `parse_timestamp` as the basis for an argparse type and store integer seconds in `args.fake_clock` (default `None`). Convert `APIError` from this argument type into `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` so invalid CLI input exits 2. T2 constructs `Clock(args.fake_clock)`; E8 uses `clock.set(validate_clock(decoded_body))`, then `format_timestamp` for its response. If T2 also accepts an unvalidated string in `run(args)`, parse it before constructing Clock. Snapshot `now = clock.now()` once per request and pass that same integer to limiter/storage.
24	
25	`linkvault.storage.Storage(path: str)` opens/creates the exact schema using a single connection with `check_same_thread=False`; all DB access/transaction completion and closure are serialized by one lock. Parent directories are not created. Exported instance methods:
26	
27	- `issue_token(now: int) -> dict`: ordered `token,created_at`; `lv_` + `secrets.token_hex(16)`; stores only full-token SHA-256 digest and integer timestamp; committed before return.
28	- `authenticate(token: str) -> str`: takes the raw token, not the Authorization header; returns its digest as an opaque owner/rate key. Malformed/unknown tokens raise 401 `unauthorized`. T2 must enforce exact single-space `Bearer <token>` header syntax before calling this.
29	- `create_link(token_hash: str, body: dict, now: int, base_url: str) -> dict`: validates complete E3 schema before checking state, generates at most five seven-character candidates using exact `secrets.choice` alphabet, commits, and returns the ordered link object. Custom duplicate/reserved lowercase `healthz` raises 409 `slug_taken`; generation exhaustion raises 500 `internal`. Expired links still occupy slugs.
30	- `list_links(token_hash: str, base_url: str) -> dict`: ordered `{"links": [...]}` including expired links, sorted by created_at then binary/case-sensitive slug.
31	- `get_link(token_hash: str, slug: str, base_url: str) -> dict`: ordered link object; unknown/foreign resource raises 404 `not_found`.
32	- `delete_link(token_hash: str, slug: str) -> None`: committed deletion; unknown/foreign resource raises 404 `not_found`; slug immediately reusable. T2 sends empty 204.
33	- `resolve(slug: str, now: int) -> str`: verbatim URL after locked lookup/expiry/exact prescribed increment SQL/commit. Unknown raises 404 `not_found`; `now >= expires_at` raises 410 `gone` without mutation. T2 sends empty 302 with exact Location. No rate limiting occurs in storage.
34	- `close() -> None`: locked connection closure; callers stop/drain request work before closing.
35	
36	`base_url` must be the actual bound origin, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:43210` without a trailing slash. Every returned link uses ordered keys `slug,url,short_url,created_at,expires_at,clicks,last_clicked_at`, with nullable fields represented by `None`. Owners are digests obtained from `authenticate`, not user-supplied identities. No database row/connection escapes the public methods.

38	## Exception/error translation and precedence
39	
40	T2 catches `APIError` and sends `error.status`, `error.headers`, `json_bytes(error.body())`; unexpected exceptions become 500 `internal` and must not expose exception text/DB details. SQLite open/initialization exceptions deliberately propagate for `server.run` startup handling (stderr, exit 3). Other SQLite errors also propagate as unexpected internal errors, not misleading 409 conflicts; failed mutation transactions roll back. T3 translates timestamp/configuration validation failures into argparse usage errors (exit 2), not HTTP JSON.
41	
42	The caller owns route404 → auth401 → limiter429 → size413 → decode400 → schema400 → resource404/409/410. Call limiter exactly once per authenticated link request after route/auth and before body size/decode/storage, regardless of later status. Do not call it for admin, health or redirects. Storage does not enforce route matching or HTTP header grammar. Raw schema dictionaries are validated inside create; E8 validation is explicit through `validate_clock`.

3	## Scope and interface
4	
5	Worker owns only `linkvault/server.py`, `tests/test_server.py`, and these notes. T3 runs concurrently in disjoint files. No CLI/client, frozen artifact, board, handoff or shared fixture changes; no commits.
6	
7	`server.run(args)` consumes `db, admin_key, port, rate_limit, fake_clock`; `fake_clock` is the T1/T3-agreed parsed integer seconds or `None`. It returns 3 on database initialization/bind failure and 0 on clean signal shutdown. `Server` is a loopback-only ThreadingHTTPServer with file-local in-process HTTP fixtures. `Handler` routes using the original request line rather than normalized `self.path`, handles arbitrary extension methods via JSON route errors, applies route/auth/rate/size/JSON/validation/state precedence and shares T1 storage/clock/limiter.
8	
9	## Unicode Location wire decision
10	
11	Valid URLs are not restricted beyond T1 R6 validation. Storage and JSON retain the original URL. For redirect Location, original Latin-1-compatible values use their original Latin-1 bytes (preserving stdlib header compatibility); values containing non-Latin-1 characters use the original value's UTF-8 bytes, emitted through the stdlib header writer without percent escaping, IDNA, normalization, or replacement. A client that decodes every header as Latin-1 must recover the raw octets and decode UTF-8 for this latter case. The contract does not specify a Unicode header charset. Focused regression tests inspect raw header bytes for ASCII, Latin-1, and CJK URLs, including Unicode hosts/paths/queries/fragments.
12	
13	## Lifecycle design and validation scope
14	
15	Signals set only a main-thread boolean. A separate thread serves; the main thread stops acceptance with shutdown(), interrupts every accepted active socket (including idle, partial headers, and incomplete bodies), joins non-daemon handler threads, then closes storage and restores signal handlers. No DB operation may outlive closure. Focused tests invoke run on the main thread with real in-process signals and local sockets; subprocess CLI/OS exit and restart acceptance remain T4 responsibility. SIGBREAK is conditionally tested and skipped when absent.

`decode_json(body: bytes) -> dict` retains its signature and object-returning API and now supplies a request-local `parse_int=_parse_int` to `json.loads`. `_parse_int` converts at most eight decimal digits (plus optional minus sign) with `int`; longer integer lexemes become the integer sentinel `31536001`.
